en: Test for English Majors, 2015.
zh: 2015年英语专业全国统一考试。

en: Grade 8.
zh: 专业八级。

en: Part 1 Listening Comprehension.
zh: 第一部分：听力理解。

en: Section A mini-lecture.
zh: A节：短讲。

en: In this section you will hear a mini-lecture.
zh: 在这一节中，你将听到一段短讲。

en: You will hear the mini-lecture once only.
zh: 这段短讲只播放一遍。

en: While listening to the mini-lecture, please complete the gap-filling task on Answer Sheet 1 and write no more than three words for each gap.
zh: 请边听短讲，边完成答题卡一上的填空任务；每空填写不超过三个词。

en: Make sure the word(s) you fill in is or are both grammatically and semantically acceptable.
zh: 请确保填入的词在语法和语义上都恰当。

en: You may use the blank sheet for note-taking.
zh: 你可以用空白纸做笔记。

en: You have thirty seconds to preview the gap-filling task.
zh: 你有三十秒钟预览填空任务。

en: Now, listen to the mini-lecture.
zh: 现在请听短讲。

en: When it is over, you will be given three minutes to check your work.
zh: 短讲结束后，你将有三分钟检查作答。

en: Understanding academic lectures.
zh: 理解学术讲座。

en: Good morning, everybody.
zh: 大家早上好。

en: Now, at the university, you, as students, are often called on to perform many types of listening tasks:
zh: 在大学里，作为学生，你们经常需要完成各种听力任务：

en: listening in a group discussion, listening to a teacher on a one-to-one basis, and listening to academic lectures.
zh: 听小组讨论、与老师一对一交谈，以及听学术讲座。

en: So what I’m going to talk about today is what a listener needs to be able to do in order to comprehend an academic lecture efficiently.
zh: 因此，今天我要讲的是，听众要具备哪些能力，才能高效地理解一场学术讲座。

en: OK.
zh: 好。

en: What do you need to do in order to understand the lecture?
zh: 要听懂讲座，你需要做些什么呢？

en: Now there are four things that I’m going to talk about.
zh: 接下来，我要谈四个方面。

en: The first thing is that you need to be aware of all of the parts of the language that carry meaning.
zh: 首先，你需要意识到，语言中所有能够传达意义的组成部分都值得注意。

en: You all know that words carry meaning.
zh: 你们都知道，词语能够传达意义。

en: So you've got to be aware of the vocabulary of the language, but there are some other features.
zh: 所以，你必须了解这门语言的词汇，但除此之外，还有其他特征。

en: For one thing, you need to be aware of stress.
zh: 例如，你需要注意重音。

en: Let me give you an example.
zh: 我来举个例子。

en: “I went to the bar.” “I went to the bar.” It makes a difference.
zh: “我去了酒吧。”“是我去了酒吧。”这样读，意思就有所不同。

en: In the second example, I’m stressing the fact that it was me and not someone else so that this means stress has some meaning.
zh: 在第二个例子里，我强调的是去酒吧的人是我，而不是别人；这就说明，重音本身也传递意义。

en: Now the next thing you might want to listen for is intonation.
zh: 接下来，你可能需要留意的是语调。

en: For example, if I say “He came.” “He came?” There are two different meanings.
zh: 比如，我说“他来了。”“他来了？”这两句话表达的是不同的意思。

en: One is a statement, the other one is a question.
zh: 一个是陈述，另一个是提问。

en: And another thing you need to listen for is rhythm.
zh: 你还需要留意节奏。

en: For instance, “Can you see, Mary?” versus “Can you see Mary?” da da DA da... da da da DA da.
zh: 比如，“玛丽，你看得见吗？”与“你看得见玛丽吗？”——哒哒哒哒……哒哒哒哒。

en: Those two mean something different.
zh: 这两种说法表达的意思不同。

en: In the first one, they are talking directly to Mary, while the second one means “Can you see Mary... over there?”
zh: 第一种说法是直接对玛丽说话，而第二种则是问：“你看得见那边的玛丽吗？”

en: Now the next thing you must do when you listen is that you need to add information that the lecturer expects you to add.
zh: 接下来，听的时候你还必须补充一些信息，而讲课人会预期你能够自行补上这些信息。

en: All lecturers assume that they share some information with their audience and that their audience does not need them to explain every word.
zh: 所有讲课人都会假定，自己与听众掌握着某些共同信息，因此不必逐字解释每个词。

en: And listeners have an ability to add this information due to two sources of information.
zh: 听众能够补充这些信息，是因为他们有两种信息来源。

en: That is, one, their knowledge of a particular subject; and, two, their knowledge or experience of the world.
zh: 第一，是对某个特定学科的了解；第二，是对世界的知识或生活经验。

en: So remember: listening is not a matter of just absorbing the speaker’s words; the listener has to do more than that.
zh: 所以，请记住：听讲并不是仅仅接收说话人的话语，听众还需要做得更多。

en: The listener is not a tape recorder, absorbing the speaker’s words and putting them into his or her brain.
zh: 听众不是录音机，不会只是接收说话人的话，再把这些话存进脑海。

en: Rather, listening involves hearing the speaker's words and reinterpreting them, adding information if necessary.
zh: 相反，听的过程包括听见说话人的话、重新理解这些话，并在必要时补充信息。

en: So the meaning is not in the word alone, rather it is in the person who uses it or responds to it so that the second thing that a listener must do—
zh: 因此，意义并不只存在于词语本身，也存在于使用这些词语、或对其作出回应的人身上。所以，听众要做的第二件事，

en: add information that the lecturer assumes that they share.
zh: 就是补充讲课人假定双方都知道的信息。

en: OK.
zh: 好。

en: The third thing that a listener needs to do, and this is to me the most important thing of all, and that’s to predict as you listen.
zh: 听众需要做的第三件事——在我看来也是最重要的一件事——就是边听边预测。

en: Now let me give you two reasons why you have to predict.
zh: 现在，我来解释为什么要预测，原因有两个。

en: For one thing, if you predict it helps you overcome noise.
zh: 首先，预测有助于你克服噪声的干扰。

en: What do I mean by noise?
zh: 这里所说的“噪声”是什么意思呢？

en: Maybe there’s noise outside and you can’t hear me.
zh: 也许外面很吵，以至于你听不见我说话。

en: Maybe you're in the back of the room and you can’t hear all that well.
zh: 也许你坐在教室后面，听得不太清楚。

en: Maybe the microphone doesn’t work.
zh: 也许麦克风出了故障。

en: Maybe there’s noise inside your head.
zh: 也许噪声来自你的脑海。

en: By that I mean maybe you're thinking of something else.
zh: 我的意思是，你可能正在想着其他事情。

en: And then all of a sudden, you'll remember “Oh, I’ve got to listen.” By being able to predict during the lecture,
zh: 随后，你会突然想起来：“哦，我得认真听。”如果你能在听讲时进行预测，

en: you can just keep listening to the lecture and not lose the idea of what’s going on.
zh: 就能继续跟上讲座，而不会失去对当前内容的理解。

en: So predicting is important to help you overcome outside noise and inside noise.
zh: 所以，预测对于克服外部噪声和内心干扰都很重要。

en: And another reason that predicting is important is because it saves you time.
zh: 预测之所以重要，还有一个原因，那就是它能节省时间。

en: Now when you listen you need time to think about the information, relate it to old ideas, take notes,
zh: 听讲时，你需要时间来思考信息、把它与已有的想法联系起来，以及记笔记；

en: and if you’re only keeping up with what I’m saying or what the lecturer’s saying, you have no time to do that.
zh: 如果你只是勉强跟上我或讲课人的讲话，就没有时间做这些事了。

en: And I’ll bet a lot of you are having that problem right now because it’s so hard just to follow everything I’m saying,
zh: 我敢说，你们中很多人现在就有这个问题：光是跟上我说的全部内容，就已经很费力了，

en: that you don’t have time to note down ideas.
zh: 因而没有时间记下要点。

en: So predicting saves you time.
zh: 因此，预测可以节省时间。

en: If you can guess what I’m going to say, you're able to take notes, you’re able to think, you have more time.
zh: 如果你能猜到我接下来会说什么，就能记笔记，也能进行思考，你就拥有更多时间。

en: OK?
zh: 明白吗？

en: And there are two types of predictions that you can make: predictions of content and predictions of organization.
zh: 你可以作出两类预测：对内容的预测，以及对组织结构的预测。

en: Let me give you an example in terms of content.
zh: 我先举一个预测内容的例子。

en: If you hear the words “Because he loved to cook, his favorite room was...” what would you expect?
zh: 如果你听到“因为他喜欢做饭，他最喜欢的房间是……”这些话，你会预期接下来出现什么词？

en: Kitchen.
zh: 厨房。

en: You can guess this because you know people cook in the kitchen.
zh: 你能猜到这一点，是因为你知道人们通常在厨房里做饭。

en: OK?
zh: 明白吗？

en: And you can also predict organization.
zh: 你也可以预测讲话的组织结构。

en: So if I was going to tell you a story, you'd expect me to tell you why the story is important, give you a setting for the story.
zh: 比如，如果我要给你讲一个故事，你就会期待我先说明这个故事为什么重要，并交代故事发生的背景。

en: So you have expectations of what the speaker is going to talk about and how the speaker will organize his or her words.
zh: 因此，对于说话人接下来要谈什么，以及他或她会如何组织语言，你都会有所预期。

en: Now let’s come to the last thing a listener must do: the listener must evaluate, as he or she is listening,
zh: 现在来看听众必须做的最后一件事：边听边评价，

en: decide what’s important, what’s not, decide how something relates to something else.
zh: 判断什么重要、什么不重要，以及某件事与另一件事之间有什么联系。

en: OK?
zh: 明白吗？

en: There are again two reasons for this.
zh: 这样做同样有两个原因。

en: The first one is evaluating helps you to decide what to take notes about: what's important to write down? what’s not important to write down?
zh: 第一个原因是，评价能够帮助你决定哪些内容值得记笔记：什么值得写下来？什么不值得写下来？

en: And the second reason is that evaluating helps you to keep information.
zh: 第二个原因是，评价有助于你记住信息。

en: Studies have shown that we retain more information if ideas are connected to one another rather than just individually remembered.
zh: 研究表明，如果各种想法彼此关联，而不是各自孤立地记忆，我们就能记住更多信息。

en: So for example, if I give you five ideas that are not related to one another, that’s much more difficult to remember than five ideas that are related.
zh: 比如，我给你五个彼此不相关的想法，它们会比五个相互关联的想法难记得多。

en: So you can see evaluating helps you to remember information better because it connects ideas to one another.
zh: 所以，你可以看到，评价把各种想法联系在一起，因此能帮助你更好地记住信息。

en: OK.
zh: 好。

en: From what I’ve said so far, you can see there’s a lot involved in listening to lectures:
zh: 从刚才的内容可以看出，听讲座涉及很多事情：

en: language awareness, adding information, making predictions and evaluations.
zh: 语言意识、补充信息、进行预测和作出评价。

en: I hope these will be useful to you in lecture comprehension.
zh: 我希望这些方法能有助于你们理解讲座。

en: Now, you have three minutes to check your work.
zh: 现在你有三分钟检查作答。

en: This is the end of Section A mini-lecture.
zh: A节短讲到此结束。
